faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
faq.q1: Are my mods kept if I switch profiles?
faq.a1: Yes! Each profile keeps its own mod state. When you return to a profile, your enabled mods are still there, even after a restart.
faq.q2: What is the difference between .MM and .JSON?
faq.a2: Technically none! .MM is simply a .JSON file renamed to make sharing between players easier.
faq.q3: What happens if I delete an enabled mod?
faq.a3: You must first disable the mod so its files are removed from the game, then you can safely delete it.
faq.q4: How do I update a mod?
faq.a4: Disable the mod, replace its files in the mods folder, then re-enable it. The backup will be recreated automatically.
faq.qPat: How do I get a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT)?
faq.aPat_intro: A Personal Access Token (PAT) lets you download more than 60 mods/hour from GitHub. Here's how to create one:
faq.aPat_s1: Log in to github.com with your account.
faq.aPat_s3: Scroll down in the left menu to Developer settings (very bottom).
faq.aPat_s6: Give it a name (e.g. BMM Downloads), choose an expiry, and check only public_repo under repo.
faq.aPat_s7: Click Generate token, copy it (it starts with ghp_) and paste it into the GitHub PAT field in BMM Settings.
faq.aPat_warn: Never share your token! It grants access to your GitHub account.
faq.q5: What happens if two mods use the same file?
faq.a5: BMM uses a stacked system. The last mod you enable has priority. But don't worry: if you disable it, BMM will automatically restore the previous mod's file or the original!
faq.q6: Can I see the mod contents without installing it?
faq.a6: Yes! Use the Archive Explorer in the mod details to navigate folders and even open files directly.
faq.q7: Why does my mod take so long to load?
faq.a7: It's often because the mod is very large (many files or several GBs). If the mods folder and the game are not on the same hard drive, copying may be slowed down by your drive speeds.
faq.q8: What happens if my disk is full?
faq.a8: BMM checks the space before each copy. If the disk is full, activation is blocked for safety, even if alerts are disabled in the settings.
faq.q9: Can I disable the disk safety limit?
faq.a9: No. Unlike visual alerts, blocking in case of a saturated disk is vital to prevent data or system corruption.

docs.enableDisableDesc:
Unlike classic mod managers that create risky or unstable virtual links (symlinks), Better Mod Manager performs a smart physical copy of your files.

1. Activation: When you enable a mod, BMM analyzes the files. If they replace original game files, it discreetly copies them to your Backup folder. Then, it injects the mod files into the game.

2. Deactivation: When you disable the mod, BMM removes the mod files from the game, then instantly restores the original files from the Backup folder. Your game returns to its pure state.

Warning: Always make sure to disable a mod from the application before physically deleting its folder, otherwise the game will keep its modification files and the backup will not be restored.
docs.basic.conflict.a1: BMM uses a stacking system. If two mods touch the same file, the last one defined takes priority.
docs.basic.conflict.a2: The application remembers everything it replaces in its local logs.
docs.basic.conflict.a3: By deactivating the « priority » mod, the previously activated mod's file is automatically restored!
docs.profileCustom.a1: You can choose a custom background image for each profile. BMM features a smart cropping tool for a perfect fit.
docs.profileCustom.a2: Identify your games at a glance by customizing the interface color and the profile card icon.
docs.profileCustom.a3: For safety, profile activation requires a double-click, preventing accidental loading while browsing.
onboard.performance.title: Performance — Why is it slow?
onboard.performance.text: Activating a mod can take time if it's very heavy (several GB). No worries, Tasky shows you that the work is in progress. Patience is the key to successful modding!
onboard.s1.title: Welcome!
onboard.s1.text: Hi! I'm Tasky, your personal assistant. Ready to transform your modding experience? Let me show you the ropes in just a few seconds.
onboard.s2.title: Profiles — Your starting point
onboard.s2.text: Let's get organized! Create dedicated profiles for each game. **Double-click** a card to activate it. To change the image, color, or folders, use the **Edit** button (the little pencil).
onboard.s3.title: Import from OvGME
onboard.s3.text: Migrating from OvGME? No worries! The "Import OvGME" button automatically retrieves your existing profiles and mods. They are copied independently.
onboard.s4.title: Library — Manage your mods
onboard.s4.text: Your headquarters. All your mods appear here. Use **'Scan'** to find everything at once, or **'Add'** to import a specific folder or archive.
onboard.s5.title: Enable and Disable a mod
onboard.s5.text: Magic or Science? The activation button copies files to the game. When disabling, BMM puts everything back cleanly thanks to the backup. Zero stress for your original installation!
onboard.s6.title: Edit and customize
onboard.s6.text: Click a mod to open its detail panel. Edit the name, version, author, add download links... Everything is saved per profile.
onboard.s7.title: .MM Lists — Easy sharing
onboard.s7.text: The .MM Lists page lets you export your complete configuration as a .MM file (it's just renamed JSON). Send it to a friend, they import and install everything in one click!
onboard.s8.title: Let's go!
onboard.s8.text: You are ready! Check the Documentation and FAQ for more details. Don't forget to visit the Credits page and join our Discord. Happy mod managing!
onboard.modding.title: How to properly organize a mod?
onboard.modding.text: For a mod to work, its folders must mirror the game's file structure. For example, if you place a file in 'Textures/skin.dds' in your mod folder, BMM will copy it exactly into the 'Textures' folder of your game. It's like navigating the game folders without actually touching anything!
onboard.integrity.title: Check Integrity
onboard.integrity.text: If a mod seems broken after a game update, use the Integrity Report. It compares your game files with the original mod files to detect any unexpected changes.
onboard.conflicts.title: Conflict Detection
onboard.conflicts.text: A red 'CONFLICT' tag appears if two active mods use the same files. Activation order is key: the last one enabled wins, but BMM restores previous files when disabling!
onboard.explorer.title: Archive Explorer
onboard.explorer.text: Need to check mod content? The 'Browse archive' button opens a full tree view with search and context menu for expert management.

docs.ioLimiterDesc:
The I/O Limiter prevents BMM from overwhelming your disks during mod operations.

Why? When you enable or disable large mods (several GBs), massive file copying can slow down your entire system — games, browser, streams.

How does it work? BMM splits each copy operation into small chunks and inserts micro-pauses between them to never exceed the speed limit you've set (in MB/s). Set 0 for unlimited speed.

Built-in Benchmark — Use the 'Benchmark Speed' button in the Storage Manager to automatically measure your disk speeds. BMM will then suggest an optimal value (≈70% of actual speed).

Cloud / NAS Storage — BMM automatically detects cloud drives (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) and network storage (NAS). It is strongly recommended to limit speed on these drives as they are generally slower.
faq.qIo: What is the Disk I/O Limiter for?
faq.aIo: It prevents BMM from copying files too fast, which could cause your PC to lag. Go to Settings → Storage Manager to adjust the speed limit per disk. You can also run a benchmark to get an automatically suggested value.
faq.qBenchValues: Why does the performance graph sometimes show a speed higher than my limit?
faq.aBenchValues: The performance graph monitors the entire disk, not just BMM. If you limit BMM to 10 MB/s, but Windows, your browser, or your antivirus use 2 MB/s in the background, the graph will show 12 MB/s. BMM always strictly respects its own internal limit.
onboard.benchmark.title: Performance & Monitoring
onboard.benchmark.text: The Performance Dashboard monitors CPU, RAM, and disk in real-time. It's the perfect tool to see exactly what's happening under the hood during your copies.
onboard.storage.title: I/O Limiter (Storage Manager)
onboard.storage.text: Limit your disk speeds during transfers to avoid system lag. BMM detects SSDs, HDDs, and even Cloud drives. A quick benchmark will help you find the ideal speed.

onboard.bg.text: Style it up! Each profile can have its own wallpaper. BMM includes a cropping tool so that everything looks perfect on your cards.
faq.qLimit: What happens if my disk is full (alerts disabled)?
faq.aLimit: Even if storage alerts are disabled, BMM constantly checks the total disk space. If there is not enough physical space to copy a mod's files, the activation will be blocked with an error message to protect your system from crashes and corruption.
